strings.name: Achille Mbembe
strings.summary: Educated in Cameroon and France, Mbembe taught in the United States, led CODESRIA in Dakar and later worked in South Africa. Through postcolonial states, race and “necropolitics,” he examines rule, violence and life. His work entered multilingual debates and won the 2024 Holberg Prize. In 2020 German critics accused his writings on Israel and the Holocaust of antisemitism; he denied the accusations. That debate and his scholarly contributions require distinct treatment.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Discussed power and world order through postcolonial theory and necropolitics research, influencing African studies and international intellectual debates.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Necropolitics
strings.highlights.h1.text: Studies power over life and death, bringing colonial violence, war and race into theoretical debate.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: History PhD, Paris 1 (1989); advanced political science diploma, Sciences Po Paris.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Intellectual work across regions
strings.highlights.h2.text: Through research, teaching and academic organization, brought African experiences into global political theory.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Holberg Prize
strings.timeline.t1.text: Honored for history and political theory spanning colonial violence, race and democracy.
strings.timeline.t2.title: German public controversy
strings.timeline.t2.text: Some politicians accused his writings of antisemitism or trivializing the Holocaust; he denied this. The festival was separately canceled because of the pandemic.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Critique of Black Reason published
strings.timeline.t3.text: The French original examined historical links among racial classification, capital and dehumanization.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Necropolitics essay
strings.timeline.t4.text: Published a theoretical analysis in Public Culture, later developing the subject in books.
strings.timeline.t5.title: On the Postcolony in English
strings.timeline.t5.text: The English edition expanded international discussion of postcolonial power and everyday life.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Moved to South Africa
strings.timeline.t6.text: After Dakar, settled in South Africa to research and teach at the University of the Witwatersrand.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Led CODESRIA
strings.timeline.t7.text: Became executive secretary of the Council for the Development of Social Science Research in Africa, serving until 2000.
strings.timeline.t8.title: History doctorate
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed doctoral training in Paris on the history of anti-colonial resistance in Cameroon.
